name: Kung Pao Chicken
description: A classic Sichuan dish featuring tender chicken, peanuts, and vegetables in a spicy, savory sauce.
chineseDescription: 经典川菜，鸡肉嫩滑，配以花生和蔬菜，酱汁香辣可口。
culturalBackground: Named after Ding Baozhen, a Qing dynasty official. The dish represents the bold, complex flavors of Sichuan cuisine with its signature 'gongbao' flavor profile.
seasonalConnection: Year-round dish, especially popular in winter for its warming properties.
historicalConnection: Qing Dynasty court cuisine that became a household staple.
steps: 【Prepare Chicken】Cut chicken breast into uniform 1-inch (2.5cm) cubes for even cooking. Place in a bowl.
【Marinate】Add 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch to the chicken. Mix well with hands or chopsticks until chicken is evenly coated. Let marinate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
【Make Sauce】In a small bowl, combine remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp water. Stir until sugar dissolves completely. Set aside.
【Prep Aromatics】Mince 3 cloves garlic and 1 inch ginger finely. Cut 2 bell peppers into 1-inch pieces. Chop 2 green onions into 1-inch lengths.
【Heat Wok】Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over HIGH heat (about 400°F/200°C). The oil is ready when it shimmers.
【Cook Chicken】Add marinated chicken in a single layer. Let sear for 30 seconds without moving, then stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
【Toast Chilies】In the same hot wok, add 4 dried red chilies. Stir constantly for 30 seconds until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them.
【Bloom Aromatics】Add minced garlic and ginger to the wok. Stir-fry rapidly for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
【Cook Vegetables】Add bell pepper pieces. Stir-fry on high heat for 2 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp.
【Combine】Return the cooked chicken to the wok. Pour the sauce mixture over everything. Toss continuously for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients evenly.
【Add Peanuts】Add 1/2 cup roasted peanuts. Toss gently for 30 seconds to warm through and coat with sauce.
【Serve】Transfer to a serving plate. Garnish with chopped green onion tops. Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
tips: Adjust the number of dried chilies based on your spice preference. Use Sichuan peppercorns for authentic numbing flavor.

name: Mapo Tofu
description: A famous Sichuan dish with silky tofu in a spicy, numbing sauce with ground pork.
chineseDescription: 著名川菜，豆腐嫩滑，配以麻辣酱汁和猪肉末。
culturalBackground: Created by Chen Mapo in Chengdu during the Qing dynasty. The name means 'pockmarked old woman's tofu', referring to its creator.
seasonalConnection: Popular year-round, especially comforting in cold weather.
historicalConnection: Qing Dynasty street food that became one of Sichuan's most famous exports.
steps: 【Prepare Tofu】Cut 400g soft tofu into 1-inch (2.5cm) cubes. Place on paper towels to drain excess moisture for 5 minutes. Handle gently as soft tofu breaks easily.
【Prep Ingredients】Mince 3 cloves garlic and 1 inch ginger finely. Chop 2 green onions. Mix 1 tsp cornstarch with 2 tsp cold water in a small bowl until smooth.
【Toast Peppercorns】Heat a dry wok over medium heat. Add 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns and toast for 30-60 seconds until fragrant. Remove and crush lightly. Set aside for garnish.
【Cook Pork】Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add 200g ground pork, breaking it apart. Cook for 3-4 minutes until browned and no longer pink.
【Add Aromatics】Add minced garlic and ginger to the pork. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
【Add Doubanjiang】Add 2 tbsp doubanjiang (fermented bean paste). Stir-fry for 1 minute until the oil turns red. This gives the dish its signature color and flavor.
【Add Liquid】Pour in 1 cup chicken stock and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Bring to a boil.
【Add Tofu】Gently slide tofu cubes into the sauce. Do not stir vigorously or tofu will break. Use a spatula to gently push tofu to submerge in sauce.
【Simmer】Simmer for 5 minutes, occasionally spooning sauce over the tofu. This allows flavors to penetrate the tofu.
【Thicken】Make a well in the center and add cornstarch mixture. Gently fold to combine without breaking tofu. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.
【Serve】Transfer to a serving bowl. Sprinkle with crushed Sichuan peppercorns and chopped green onions. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
tips: Handle tofu gently to keep cubes intact. Toast Sichuan peppercorns for maximum numbing effect.

name: Sweet and Sour Pork
description: Crispy pork pieces coated in a tangy sweet and sour sauce with colorful vegetables.
chineseDescription: 外酥里嫩的猪肉配以酸甜可口的酱汁和彩色蔬菜。
culturalBackground: A Cantonese classic that exemplifies the cuisine's balance of flavors. Often served at celebrations and family gatherings.
seasonalConnection: Popular for festivals and celebrations, especially Lunar New Year.
historicalConnection: Adapted from traditional sweet-sour fish dishes to use more affordable pork.
steps: 【Cut Pork】Cut 500g pork tenderloin into 2-inch long, 1/2-inch thick strips. Uniform size ensures even cooking.
【Make Batter】In a bowl, whisk 1 egg with 2 tbsp flour and 2 tbsp cornstarch. Add a pinch of salt. The batter should be thick enough to coat the pork.
【Coat Pork】Dredge pork strips in remaining 1/2 cup cornstarch, shaking off excess. Then dip into batter. The double coating creates extra crispiness.
【Heat Oil】Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C). Test by dropping a small piece of batter - it should sizzle and rise to the surface immediately.
【First Fry】Carefully add pork pieces in batches. Fry for 3-4 minutes until golden and cooked through. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove and drain on paper towels.
【Second Fry】Increase oil temperature to 400°F (200°C). Fry pork again for 30-60 seconds until extra crispy. This double-fry technique ensures maximum crunch.
【Make Sauce】In a saucepan, combine 1/2 cup ketchup, 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar, and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
【Thicken Sauce】Add 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water to the sauce. Stir until thickened and glossy. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.
【Cook Vegetables】Add pineapple cubes and bell pepper to the sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp.
【Combine】Add the crispy pork to the sauce. Toss quickly to coat evenly. Serve immediately to maintain crispiness.
【Serve】Transfer to a serving plate. Serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Double-fry the pork for extra crispiness. Add sauce just before serving to maintain crunch.

name: Yangzhou Fried Rice
description: A classic Chinese fried rice with shrimp, ham, and vegetables.
chineseDescription: 经典中式炒饭，配以虾仁、火腿和蔬菜。
culturalBackground: One of China's most famous fried rice varieties, originating from Yangzhou. Known for its 'golden silver' appearance with eggs and shrimp.
seasonalConnection: Year-round staple, perfect for using leftover rice.
historicalConnection: Ming Dynasty imperial cuisine that became a household classic.
steps: 【Prep Rice】Use cold, day-old rice for best results. Break up any clumps with your hands. Cold rice separates better during stir-frying.
【Prep Ingredients】Dice 50g Chinese ham into small cubes. Peel and devein 100g shrimp. Beat 2 eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
【Scramble Eggs】Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Pour in beaten eggs. Scramble quickly until just set but still moist. Remove and set aside.
【Cook Shrimp】Add 1 tbsp oil to the wok. Add shrimp and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until pink and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
【Stir-fry Rice】Add remaining 1 tbsp oil to the wok. Add the rice and stir-fry over high heat for 2-3 minutes. Use a spatula to break up any remaining clumps.
【Add Ham and Vegetables】Add diced ham, peas, and corn to the rice. Stir-fry for another 2 minutes until vegetables are heated through.
【Season】Add 2 tbsp soy sauce and toss to coat the rice evenly. The rice should have a light golden color.
【Combine All】Return the eggs and shrimp to the wok. Add chopped green onions. Toss everything together for 1 minute.
【Finish】Drizzle with 1 tbsp sesame oil. Give a final toss. Transfer to a serving plate and serve hot.
tips: Use day-old rice for best texture. High heat and quick stirring gives authentic wok hei flavor.

name: Pork Dumplings
description: Traditional Chinese dumplings with juicy pork filling.
chineseDescription: 传统中式饺子，馅料鲜美多汁。
culturalBackground: Dumplings symbolize wealth and prosperity due to their resemblance to ancient Chinese gold ingots. Essential for Lunar New Year celebrations.
seasonalConnection: Essential for Lunar New Year (Spring Festival) and Winter Solstice.
historicalConnection: Over 1800 years old, attributed to Zhang Zhongjing in the Eastern Han Dynasty.
steps: 【Make Dough】Mix 500g flour with 250ml warm water gradually. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
【Prepare Cabbage】Mince 200g Napa cabbage finely. Sprinkle with 1/2 tsp salt and let sit for 10 minutes. Squeeze out excess moisture.
【Make Filling】Combine ground pork, squeezed cabbage, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Mix in one direction until sticky and well combined.
【Divide Dough】Roll the dough into a long log. Cut into 30 equal pieces. Cover unused pieces with a damp cloth to prevent drying.
【Wrap Dumplings】Roll each piece into a 3-inch circle. Place 1 tbsp filling in the center. Fold and pleat the edges to seal. Practice makes perfect!
【Boil Water】Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 1 tsp salt.
【Cook Dumplings】Gently slide dumplings into boiling water. Stir gently to prevent sticking. Bring to a boil, then add 1/2 cup cold water. Repeat this process 3 times.
【Check Doneness】Dumplings are done when they float to the surface and the skin looks slightly translucent. The filling should reach 165°F (74°C).
【Serve】Remove with a slotted spoon. Serve immediately with dipping sauce of vinegar, soy sauce, and chili oil.
tips: Add cold water during boiling to ensure the filling cooks through without overcooking the wrapper.

name: Xiaolongbao
description: Delicate soup dumplings filled with pork and rich broth.
chineseDescription: 精致的汤包，内含猪肉和浓郁汤汁。
culturalBackground: A Shanghai dim sum masterpiece. The soup inside is created by wrapping aspic (gelatinized broth) in the filling, which melts during steaming.
seasonalConnection: Popular year-round as dim sum, especially for weekend family gatherings.
historicalConnection: Originated in Nanxiang, Shanghai suburbs during the Qing Dynasty.
steps: 【Make Dough】Mix 300g flour with 150ml hot water. Knead until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes. The hot water makes the dough more pliable.
【Prepare Filling】Combine ground pork, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, and white pepper. Mix well in one direction.
【Add Aspic】Fold in 100g cubed pork skin aspic gently. The aspic will melt during steaming, creating the signature soup inside.
【Divide Dough】Roll dough into a log and cut into 20 equal pieces. Keep covered to prevent drying.
【Wrap】Roll each piece into a thin 4-inch circle. Place filling in center. Pleat edges while twisting top to seal. Leave a small opening at top.
【Steam】Place dumplings in a bamboo steamer lined with cabbage leaves. Steam over boiling water for 8-10 minutes.
【Serve】Serve immediately in the steamer. Be careful when biting - hot soup inside! Dip in ginger vinegar.
tips: The key is the aspic which creates soup inside. Eat carefully - bite a small hole first to release steam.

name: Peking Duck
description: An iconic Beijing dish featuring crispy duck skin and tender meat served with thin pancakes.
chineseDescription: 北京标志性菜肴，鸭皮酥脆，肉质鲜嫩，配以薄饼。
culturalBackground: China's most famous culinary export. The duck is roasted until the skin is perfectly crispy, then carved tableside and served with thin pancakes.
seasonalConnection: Popular for special occasions and banquets year-round.
historicalConnection: Imperial court cuisine dating back to the Yuan Dynasty, perfected in Ming Dynasty.
steps: 【Clean Duck】Remove giblets and excess fat from cavity. Rinse thoroughly inside and out. Pat completely dry with paper towels.
【Air Dry】Hang duck in a cool, ventilated place for 12-24 hours. This dries the skin for maximum crispiness.
【Prepare Glaze】Mix honey with 2 tbsp hot water and soy sauce. Brush evenly over duck skin.
【Season Inside】Rub five-spice powder inside the cavity. Seal openings with bamboo skewers.
【Roast】Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Place duck on a rack over a roasting pan with water. Roast for 1 hour, turning occasionally.
【Check Doneness】Skin should be deeply golden and crispy. Internal temperature at thickest part should reach 165°F (74°C).
【Rest】Let duck rest for 10 minutes before carving. This allows juices to redistribute.
【Carve】Using a sharp knife, slice skin into thin strips. Then slice meat. Serve skin and meat separately.
【Prepare Pancakes】Steam Mandarin pancakes until warm and pliable. Cut green onions into brushes.
【Serve】Spread hoisin sauce on pancake. Add duck skin, meat, cucumber, and green onion. Roll up and enjoy.
tips: Air-drying the duck is crucial for crispy skin. Use a fan to speed up the process if needed.

name: Char Siu
description: Sweet and savory Cantonese BBQ pork with a glossy red glaze.
chineseDescription: 广式烧腊，猪肉甜香，外皮红亮。
culturalBackground: The quintessential Cantonese BBQ meat. The name 'char siu' means 'fork roasted', referring to the traditional cooking method.
seasonalConnection: Year-round dim sum staple, popular for weekend family meals.
historicalConnection: Ancient Chinese roasting techniques refined in Guangdong.
steps: 【Cut Pork】Cut 500g pork shoulder into long strips, about 2 inches thick. This ensures even cooking.
【Make Marinade】Combine hoisin sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, honey, five-spice powder, Shaoxing wine, and a drop of red food coloring if using.
【Marinate】Coat pork thoroughly with marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. Turn occasionally.
【Preheat Oven】Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with foil and place a rack on top.
【Roast First Side】Place pork on rack. Roast for 12-15 minutes until starting to caramelize.
【Turn and Baste】Turn pork over. Baste with remaining marinade. Roast another 10-12 minutes.
【Glaze】Brush with honey. Broil for 2-3 minutes until charred edges appear. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
【Rest】Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes. This allows juices to redistribute.
【Slice and Serve】Slice against the grain into thin pieces. Serve with steamed rice or in bao buns.
tips: For authentic charred edges, finish under the broiler. The pork should have a glossy, caramelized exterior.

name: Sichuan Hot Pot
description: A communal dining experience with a bubbling spicy broth for cooking various ingredients.
chineseDescription: 聚餐体验，沸腾的麻辣汤底煮各种食材。
culturalBackground: More than a dish, hot pot is a social experience. Friends gather around the bubbling pot, cooking and chatting together.
seasonalConnection: Especially popular in winter for its warming properties.
historicalConnection: Originated from Mongol cavalry cooking methods, adapted in Sichuan with local spices.
steps: 【Prepare Broth】Empty hot pot soup base into a large pot. Add 1.5L water or chicken stock. Bring to a boil.
【Prep Ingredients】Slice all meats paper-thin for quick cooking. Cut vegetables into bite-sized pieces. Arrange on platters.
【Set Up Station】Place hot pot in center of table with portable burner. Keep broth at a steady simmer.
【Prepare Dipping Sauces】Set up a sauce station with sesame oil, garlic, chili oil, soy sauce, and vinegar. Let guests create their own blends.
【Cook Meat】Dip thinly sliced meat into broth for 10-15 seconds until just cooked. Do not overcook.
【Cook Seafood】Fish and shrimp need 1-2 minutes. Watch for color change to indicate doneness.
【Cook Vegetables】Add leafy greens last as they cook quickly. Heartier vegetables like lotus root need 3-4 minutes.
【Enjoy Noodles】Add glass noodles to broth at the end to soak up flavors. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
【Refill Broth】Keep extra hot water nearby to replenish evaporated broth. Adjust seasoning as needed.
tips: Cook ingredients in order: meat first, then seafood, then vegetables. Don't overcrowd the pot.

name: Century Egg Congee
description: Creamy rice porridge topped with century egg and shredded pork.
chineseDescription: 绵滑的白粥配以皮蛋和瘦肉。
culturalBackground: The ultimate Chinese comfort food. Congee is eaten for breakfast across China, with regional variations in toppings.
seasonalConnection: Year-round breakfast staple, especially comforting when ill.
historicalConnection: Ancient Chinese grain porridge, dating back thousands of years.
steps: 【Wash Rice】Rinse 1 cup rice until water runs clear. This removes excess starch for cleaner flavor.
【Start Congee】Bring 8 cups water or stock to a boil. Add rice and stir to prevent sticking.
【Simmer】Reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally. The rice should break down completely.
【Cook Pork】Season shredded pork with a pinch of salt. Add to congee during last 15 minutes of cooking.
【Check Consistency】Congee should be thick and creamy. Add more water if too thick, or cook longer if too thin.
【Add Century Eggs】Add diced century eggs during last 5 minutes. Gently stir to distribute.
【Season】Add 1 tbsp soy sauce and white pepper to taste.
【Serve】Ladle into bowls. Top with julienned ginger and chopped green onions. Drizzle with sesame oil.
tips: Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Frozen rice breaks down faster for quicker congee.

name: Braised Pork Belly
description: Tender, melt-in-your-mouth pork belly braised in soy sauce and sugar.
chineseDescription: 五花肉酥烂入味，色泽红亮。
culturalBackground: Perhaps China's most beloved pork dish. The red color comes from caramelized sugar and soy sauce, symbolizing prosperity.
seasonalConnection: Popular for festivals and family gatherings, especially Lunar New Year.
historicalConnection: Associated with Su Dongpo, the Song Dynasty poet who perfected the recipe.
steps: 【Cut Pork】Cut 600g pork belly into 1.5-inch cubes. Uniform size ensures even cooking.
【Blanch】Bring a pot of water to boil. Add pork and boil for 3 minutes. Remove, rinse, and drain. This removes impurities.
【Caramelize Sugar】Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over medium heat. Add 3 tbsp rock sugar. Stir until melted and amber colored.
【Sear Pork】Add pork cubes to caramelized sugar. Toss to coat evenly. The sugar gives the pork its signature red color.
【Add Aromatics】Add ginger slices, star anise, and cinnamon sticks. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
【Add Liquid】Add Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and water. Liquid should almost cover the pork.
【Simmer】Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer covered for 1.5-2 hours until pork is fork-tender.
【Reduce Sauce】Remove lid for last 15 minutes. Increase heat to reduce sauce until thick and glossy.
【Serve】Transfer to a serving plate. Pour sauce over pork. Serve with steamed white rice.
tips: The key is patient slow-cooking. Rock sugar gives a beautiful sheen and subtle sweetness.

name: Scrambled Eggs with Tomatoes
description: A beloved Chinese home-style dish with fluffy eggs and sweet-tangy tomatoes.
chineseDescription: 家常菜，鸡蛋松软，番茄酸甜可口。
culturalBackground: The quintessential Chinese comfort food. Every home cook has their own version of this dish.
seasonalConnection: Year-round staple, especially popular in summer when tomatoes are peak.
historicalConnection: Modern Chinese home cooking, became popular after tomatoes were introduced to China.
steps: 【Prep Tomatoes】Cut 3 tomatoes into wedges. Set aside.
【Beat Eggs】Beat 4 eggs with 1/2 tsp salt. Mix well until uniform.
【Cook Eggs】Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Pour in eggs. When edges set, push toward center. Repeat until eggs are just set but still moist. Remove and set aside.
【Cook Tomatoes】Add a little more oil to wok. Add tomato wedges. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until softened and juices release.
【Season】Add 1 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp salt. Sugar balances the tomato acidity.
【Combine】Return eggs to wok. Gently fold together. Do not overcook or eggs become tough.
【Finish】Drizzle with sesame oil. Garnish with chopped green onions.
【Serve】Serve immediately with steamed rice. This is ultimate comfort food.
tips: Cook eggs until just set for fluffiest texture. Add sugar to balance tomato acidity.

name: Steamed Fish
description: Delicate steamed whole fish topped with ginger, scallions, and hot oil.
chineseDescription: 清蒸全鱼，配以姜丝、葱丝和热油。
culturalBackground: The ultimate test of a Cantonese chef. Steaming preserves the fish's natural sweetness and texture.
seasonalConnection: Essential for Lunar New Year - fish symbolizes abundance (年年有余).
historicalConnection: Classic Cantonese technique emphasizing natural flavors.
steps: 【Clean Fish】Scale and gut fish. Score both sides diagonally 2-3 times. Rinse and pat dry thoroughly.
【Set Up Steamer】Bring water to a boil in a wok or steamer. Use a heat-proof plate that fits inside.
【Place Fish】Place fish on plate. Put some ginger inside cavity. The ginger removes fishy odors.
【Steam】Place plate in steamer. Cover and steam for 10-12 minutes per pound. Fish is done when flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
【Drain Liquid】Carefully remove plate. Drain accumulated liquid - this liquid can be fishy.
【Add Toppings】Top fish with remaining julienned ginger and green onions.
【Heat Oil】Heat vegetable oil until smoking hot. Carefully pour hot oil over ginger and green onions. This cooks them instantly and releases aroma.
【Add Soy Sauce】Pour 3 tbsp soy sauce around the fish (not directly on top). Drizzle with sesame oil.
【Serve】Garnish with cilantro. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
tips: Do not overcook. Fish should be just cooked through for maximum tenderness.

name: Twice-Cooked Pork
description: Sichuan classic with pork belly first boiled, then stir-fried with fermented bean paste.
chineseDescription: 川菜代表，五花肉先煮后炒，配以豆瓣酱和蒜苗。
culturalBackground: One of Sichuan's most famous dishes. The 'twice-cooked' method ensures tender meat with concentrated flavor.
seasonalConnection: Year-round favorite, especially popular for family dinners.
historicalConnection: Traditional Sichuan home cooking passed down through generations.
steps: 【Boil Pork】Place pork belly in cold water. Bring to boil and simmer for 20 minutes until cooked through but not falling apart.
【Cool and Slice】Let pork cool slightly. Slice into thin 2-inch pieces. The meat should hold its shape.
【Prep Vegetables】Slice leeks diagonally. Cut green peppers into strips. Slice garlic and ginger.
【Render Fat】Heat wok over medium heat. Add pork slices and cook until fat renders and edges curl slightly. Remove pork.
【Stir-fry Aromatics】Add oil to rendered fat. Add doubanjiang and stir-fry until oil turns red.
【Add Vegetables】Add garlic, ginger, and green peppers. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
【Return Pork】Add pork back to wok. Add sweet bean paste, soy sauce, and sugar.
【Add Leeks】Add leeks and stir-fry for 1 minute until just wilted.
【Serve】Transfer to plate. Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Don't overcook the pork in the first boil - it should still be firm. The second cooking adds flavor.

name: Fish-Flavored Pork Shreds
description: Classic Sichuan dish with shredded pork in 'fish-flavor' sauce - no fish involved!
chineseDescription: 经典川菜，肉丝配以鱼香调味，酸甜辣俱全。
culturalBackground: The 'fish flavor' comes from the seasoning combination used in Sichuan fish dishes, applied here to pork.
seasonalConnection: Year-round favorite in Sichuan restaurants.
historicalConnection: Innovative Sichuan cooking applying fish-seasoning to other ingredients.
steps: 【Shred Pork】Cut pork loin into thin matchsticks. Marinate with 1 tsp soy sauce and cornstarch.
【Prep Vegetables】Soak wood ear mushrooms and shred. Cut bamboo shoots into matchsticks.
【Make Sauce】Mix 1 tbsp soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, and 1 tsp cornstarch with 2 tbsp water.
【Stir-fry Pork】Heat wok over high heat. Add oil and pork. Stir-fry until just cooked. Remove.
【Bloom Aromatics】Add oil to wok. Add pickled chili paste, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry until fragrant.
【Add Vegetables】Add wood ear and bamboo shoots. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
【Combine】Return pork to wok. Pour in sauce. Toss until thickened.
【Finish】Add green onions. Toss briefly. Serve with rice.
tips: The key is the pickled chili paste - it gives the authentic fish-flavor profile.

name: Dan Dan Noodles
description: Sichuan street food noodles with spicy sesame sauce and ground pork.
chineseDescription: 四川街头小吃，面条配以麻辣芝麻酱和肉末。
culturalBackground: Named after the carrying pole (dan dan) used by street vendors. A Chengdu street food icon.
seasonalConnection: Year-round street food favorite.
historicalConnection: 19th century Chengdu street food, named after vendors' carrying poles.
steps: 【Cook Pork】Heat oil in wok. Add ground pork and stir-fry until browned. Season with soy sauce.
【Make Sauce】Mix sesame paste with 2 tbsp hot water. Add chili oil, soy sauce, and Sichuan pepper powder.
【Cook Noodles】Boil noodles according to package directions. Reserve some cooking water.
【Assemble】Place sauce in serving bowl. Add a ladle of noodle cooking water. Mix well.
【Add Noodles】Add drained noodles to bowl. Toss to coat.
【Top】Top with ground pork, pickled mustard greens, garlic, and green onions.
【Serve】Mix thoroughly before eating. Enjoy the numbing, spicy, nutty flavors.
tips: Adjust chili oil and Sichuan pepper to your taste. The sauce should coat every strand.

name: Wonton Soup
description: Delicate shrimp and pork dumplings in clear broth.
chineseDescription: 精致的虾肉猪肉馄饨配以清汤。
culturalBackground: A Cantonese dim sum classic. The thin wrapper and generous filling showcase the chef's skill.
seasonalConnection: Year-round comfort food, popular for breakfast and late-night snacks.
historicalConnection: Ancient Chinese dumpling variety, regional variations across China.
steps: 【Make Filling】Combine minced shrimp, pork, sesame oil, and white pepper. Mix until sticky.
【Wrap Wontons】Place 1 tsp filling in center of wrapper. Fold into triangle, then bring corners together.
【Make Broth】Bring chicken broth to simmer. Season with salt and white pepper.
【Cook Wontons】Drop wontons into boiling water. Cook 3-4 minutes until they float.
【Serve】Ladle broth into bowls. Add wontons. Garnish with green onions and cilantro.
tips: Don't overfill the wrappers. Seal edges with a little water for tight closure.

name: Beef Chow Fun
description: Wide rice noodles stir-fried with beef and bean sprouts.
chineseDescription: 宽河粉配以牛肉和豆芽快炒。
culturalBackground: A Cantonese stir-fry classic requiring high heat and quick hands. The 'wok hei' (breath of the wok) is essential.
seasonalConnection: Year-round dim sum and late-night food favorite.
historicalConnection: Guangzhou street food that became a dim sum staple.
steps: 【Prep Noodles】Separate rice noodles gently to prevent breaking.
【Marinate Beef】Slice beef thin against grain. Marinate with light soy sauce and cornstarch.
【High Heat】Heat wok until smoking. Add oil.
【Sear Beef】Add beef and sear quickly. Remove when just cooked.
【Stir-fry Noodles】Add more oil. Add noodles and dark soy sauce. Toss over high heat.
【Add Vegetables】Add bean sprouts and green onions. Toss briefly.
【Return Beef】Add beef back. Toss everything together.
【Serve】Serve immediately while hot and smoky.
tips: High heat is essential for wok hei. Don't overcook the noodles or they'll break.

name: Har Gow
description: Crystal shrimp dumplings with translucent wrapper.
chineseDescription: 晶莹剔透的虾饺，皮薄馅鲜。
culturalBackground: The crown jewel of Cantonese dim sum. The translucent wrapper showcases the pink shrimp inside.
seasonalConnection: Weekend dim sum tradition in Guangdong and Hong Kong.
historicalConnection: Qing Dynasty teahouse specialty, perfected in Guangzhou.
steps: 【Make Dough】Mix wheat starch and tapioca starch. Pour in boiling water. Mix until smooth.
【Make Filling】Combine chopped shrimp, bamboo shoots, salt, sugar, and oil.
【Wrap】Roll dough thin. Cut circles. Place filling and pleat edges.
【Steam】Steam for 6-8 minutes until translucent.
【Serve】Serve immediately in bamboo steamer.
tips: The dough must be handled quickly while warm. Overworking makes it tough.

name: Siu Mai
description: Open-topped pork and shrimp dumplings.
chineseDescription: 开口的猪肉虾肉烧卖，顶上点缀蟹籽。
culturalBackground: A dim sum basket essential. The open top showcases the filling and garnish.
seasonalConnection: Weekend dim sum staple.
historicalConnection: Mongol-influenced dumpling adapted in Guangdong.
steps: 【Make Filling】Combine pork, shrimp, oyster sauce, and sesame oil. Mix until sticky.
【Shape】Place wrapper in palm. Add filling. Gather edges to form cup shape.
【Garnish】Top with crab roe.
【Steam】Steam for 8-10 minutes.
【Serve】Serve hot in steamer.
tips: Don't seal the top - the open shape is characteristic.

name: Roast Pigeon
description: Crispy-skinned roast pigeon, a Guangdong specialty.
chineseDescription: 皮脆肉嫩的烤乳鸽，广东名菜。
culturalBackground: A Guangdong banquet delicacy. The small bird is eaten whole, bones and all, for maximum flavor.
seasonalConnection: Special occasion dish, popular for birthdays and celebrations.
historicalConnection: Zhongshan specialty that spread throughout Guangdong.
steps: 【Clean】Clean pigeons thoroughly. Blanch in boiling water.
【Marinate】Rub inside and out with five-spice and soy sauce. Marinate 1 hour.
【Dry** Hang to dry 30 minutes.
【Glaze** Brush with maltose solution.
【Roast** Roast at 400°F for 15 minutes until skin is crispy.
【Serve** Serve whole. Eat bones and all for authentic experience.
tips: The pigeon should be young (squab) for tender meat.

name: Claypot Rice
description: Rice cooked in clay pot with sausage and chicken, topped with crispy rice.
chineseDescription: 砂锅煮饭配以腊肠和鸡肉，锅底有香脆锅巴。
culturalBackground: Guangzhou street food favorite. The clay pot creates a crispy rice crust at the bottom.
seasonalConnection: Especially popular in winter for its warming properties.
historicalConnection: Traditional Guangdong home cooking method.
steps: 【Soak Rice】Soak rice 30 minutes. Drain.
【Start Rice** Add rice and water to clay pot. Bring to boil.
【Add Toppings** When water is almost absorbed, add sausage and chicken.
【Steam** Cover and cook on low 15 minutes.
【Season** Drizzle with soy sauce and oyster sauce.
【Crisp** Increase heat briefly to create crispy bottom.
【Serve** Top with green onions. Mix before eating.
tips: Listen for the sizzling sound - that means the crispy rice is forming.

name: Lion's Head Meatballs
description: Large, tender pork meatballs braised with bok choy.
chineseDescription: 大而嫩的猪肉丸子配以青菜红烧。
culturalBackground: A Huaiyang cuisine classic. The name comes from the meatball's resemblance to a lion's head with the vegetable as mane.
seasonalConnection: Traditional Spring Festival dish in Jiangsu.
historicalConnection: Famous Yangzhou dish dating back to Sui Dynasty.
steps: 【Mix Meat】Combine pork, green onions, ginger, egg, soy sauce, and wine. Mix until sticky.
【Shape** Form into 4 large meatballs.
【Sear** Brown meatballs in oil. Remove.
【Cook Vegetables** Add bok choy to pot. Cook briefly.
【Braise** Return meatballs. Add broth. Simmer 45 minutes.
【Serve** Serve meatballs over bok choy with sauce.
tips: Use fatty pork for tender meatballs. Handle gently to keep shape.

name: Wuxi Sweet Ribs
description: Wuxi specialty pork ribs with sweet red glaze.
chineseDescription: 无锡名菜，排骨酥烂，色泽红亮，口味甜香。
culturalBackground: Wuxi's signature dish. The sweet glaze reflects the Jiangnan preference for slightly sweet flavors.
seasonalConnection: Popular for festivals and family gatherings.
historicalConnection: Wuxi specialty since early 20th century.
steps: 【Cut Ribs** Cut ribs into individual pieces.
【Blanch** Blanch ribs in boiling water. Drain.
【Caramelize** Melt rock sugar in oil until amber.
【Sear** Add ribs and coat in caramel.
【Braise** Add soy sauce, vinegar, wine, star anise, cinnamon, and water. Simmer 1 hour.
【Reduce** Increase heat to thicken sauce.
【Serve** Serve with sauce drizzled over.
tips: The balance of sweet and sour is key. Don't rush the caramelization.

name: Beggar's Chicken
description: Chicken wrapped in lotus leaf and clay, baked to aromatic perfection.
chineseDescription: 荷叶包裹泥土烘烤的鸡，香气扑鼻。
culturalBackground: Legend says a beggar wrapped a stolen chicken in mud and baked it, creating this delicious dish.
seasonalConnection: Special occasion dish, impressive for dinner parties.
historicalConnection: Changshu legend dating back centuries.
steps: 【Season Chicken** Rub chicken with soy sauce and wine. Stuff with mushrooms and bamboo shoots.
【Wrap** Wrap chicken in lotus leaf.
【Clay** Cover with clay or salt dough, sealing completely.
【Bake** Bake at 350°F for 3 hours.
【Crack** Break open clay at table.
【Serve** Unwrap and serve the aromatic chicken.
tips: The clay seals in all moisture and flavor. A dramatic presentation.

name: Dongpo Pork
description: Braised pork belly attributed to poet Su Dongpo.
chineseDescription: 相传为苏东坡所创，红烧肉酥烂入味。
culturalBackground: Named after Song Dynasty poet Su Dongpo, who supposedly invented this dish while exiled in Hangzhou.
seasonalConnection: Hangzhou specialty, popular year-round.
historicalConnection: Song Dynasty literary cuisine, named after poet Su Shi.
steps: 【Blanch** Blanch pork belly. Cut into 2-inch cubes.
【Layer** Place green onions and ginger in pot bottom. Add pork skin-side down.
【Add Liquid** Pour in wine, soy sauce, and rock sugar. Add water to cover.
【Braise** Simmer 2 hours until meltingly tender.
【Serve** Serve in small bowls, one piece per person.
tips: Use quality Shaoxing wine for authentic flavor. The meat should fall apart.

name: West Lake Vinegar Fish
description: Steamed fish in sweet-sour vinegar sauce, a Hangzhou classic.
chineseDescription: 杭州名菜，清蒸鱼配以酸甜醋汁。
culturalBackground: Hangzhou's signature dish, featuring the local grass carp from West Lake.
seasonalConnection: Must-try for Hangzhou tourists year-round.
historicalConnection: Song Dynasty Hangzhou cuisine, named after West Lake.
steps: 【Clean Fish** Clean and score fish diagonally.
【Steam** Steam fish 8-10 minutes until just cooked.
【Make Sauce** Heat vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce. Thicken with cornstarch.
【Pour** Pour hot sauce over fish.
【Garnish** Top with ginger and green onions.
tips: Don't overcook the fish. The sauce should be sweet-tart, not heavy.

name: Longjing Shrimp
description: Shrimp stir-fried with famous Longjing tea leaves.
chineseDescription: 龙井茶叶配以鲜虾仁清炒，清香扑鼻。
culturalBackground: Hangzhou specialty combining the city's famous tea with fresh river shrimp.
seasonalConnection: Best in spring when Longjing tea is fresh.
historicalConnection: Qing Dynasty imperial cuisine, inspired by Emperor Qianlong.
steps: 【Brew Tea** Steep tea leaves in hot water. Set aside.
【Marinate Shrimp** Coat shrimp with egg white and cornstarch.
【Blanch** Briefly blanch shrimp in hot oil. Drain.
【Stir-fry** Heat clean oil. Add shrimp and tea leaves.
【Season** Add salt and a splash of tea liquid.
【Serve** Serve immediately while fragrant.
tips: Use fresh Longjing tea for best flavor. Don't overcook the delicate shrimp.

name: Stinky Tofu
description: Fermented tofu deep-fried until crispy outside, soft inside.
chineseDescription: 发酵豆腐油炸至外酥里嫩，闻着臭吃着香。
culturalBackground: Changsha's most famous street food. The smell is notorious but the taste is beloved.
seasonalConnection: Year-round street food, especially popular as night snack.
historicalConnection: Qing Dynasty street food, loved by Empress Cixi.
steps: 【Ferment** Soak tofu in fermented brine for several days.
【Cut** Cut into 2-inch squares.
【Fry** Deep fry at 350°F until golden and crispy.
【Serve** Serve with chili sauce and pickled vegetables.
tips: The smell is intense but the taste is mild. A must-try for adventurous eaters.

name: Steamed Chicken with Mushrooms
description: Tender steamed chicken with shiitake mushrooms.
chineseDescription: 嫩滑鸡肉配以香菇清蒸。
culturalBackground: Classic Cantonese home cooking. Steaming keeps the chicken moist and tender.
seasonalConnection: Year-round family dinner staple.
historicalConnection: Traditional Cantonese cooking method.
steps: 【Marinate** Marinate chicken with oyster sauce, ginger, and cornstarch.
【Add Mushrooms** Add mushrooms and mix.
【Steam** Steam for 15-20 minutes.
【Garnish** Top with green onions.
【Serve** Serve with rice.
tips: Don't over-steam or chicken becomes tough.

name: Sour and Spicy Shredded Potatoes
description: Crisp shredded potatoes in vinegar and chili.
chineseDescription: 土豆丝配以醋和辣椒快炒，酸辣爽脆。
culturalBackground: A Northern Chinese home-style classic. The potatoes stay crisp with quick cooking.
seasonalConnection: Year-round staple, especially popular in winter.
historicalConnection: Modern Chinese home cooking, showcasing potato as staple.
steps: 【Julienne** Cut potatoes into thin matchsticks. Rinse to remove starch.
【Heat Wok** Heat oil until smoking.
【Bloom Chilies** Add chilies and garlic. Stir-fry briefly.
【Add Potatoes** Add potatoes. Stir-fry on high heat.
【Season** Add vinegar and salt. Toss quickly.
【Serve** Serve immediately while crisp.
tips: Rinse potatoes well for crispness. Cook quickly on high heat.

name: Braised Beef Noodles
description: Hand-pulled noodles in rich beef broth with tender beef.
chineseDescription: 手工拉面配以浓郁牛肉汤和酥烂牛肉。
culturalBackground: Lanzhou's famous beef noodles are a Northwest China icon. The clear broth and hand-pulled noodles are legendary.
seasonalConnection: Year-round staple, especially warming in winter.
historicalConnection: Lanzhou Muslim cuisine, over 100 years old.
steps: 【Braise Beef** Braise beef with star anise, peppercorns, and ginger for 2 hours.
【Slice** Slice beef thin.
【Cook Noodles** Pull and boil noodles until al dente.
【Assemble** Place noodles in bowl. Ladle hot broth over.
**Top with beef, chili oil, and cilantro.
tips: The broth should be clear and aromatic. Hand-pulled noodles are ideal.

name: Zhajiang Noodles
description: Beijing noodles with rich pork and fermented bean sauce.
chineseDescription: 北京炸酱面，面条配以浓郁肉酱和菜码。
culturalBackground: Beijing's signature noodle dish. The rich sauce coats thick hand-cut noodles.
seasonalConnection: Year-round Beijing staple, especially popular in summer.
historicalConnection: Beijing home cooking tradition for generations.
steps: 【Make Sauce** Brown pork. Add bean sauces and simmer until thick.
【Cook Noodles** Boil noodles until al dente.
**Prep Vegetables** Julienne cucumber. Blanch bean sprouts.
**Assemble** Toss noodles with sauce. Top with vegetables.
tips: The sauce should be rich and coat the noodles well.

name: Hot Dry Noodles
description: Wuhan breakfast noodles with sesame paste and chili oil.
chineseDescription: 武汉早餐代表，碱面配以芝麻酱和辣油。
culturalBackground: Wuhan's iconic breakfast. Every Wuhan local starts their day with a bowl.
seasonalConnection: Year-round breakfast staple in Wuhan.
historicalConnection: Wuhan street food since early 20th century.
steps: 【Cook Noodles** Boil noodles. Drain briefly.
**Make Sauce** Mix sesame paste with hot water, soy sauce, and chili oil.
**Toss** Toss noodles with sauce.
**Top with pickled vegetables and green onions.
tips: The sesame paste should be loose enough to coat noodles evenly.

name: Stewed Pork Buns
description: Xi'an specialty: crispy bun stuffed with tender stewed pork.
chineseDescription: 西安名吃，白吉馍夹酥烂腊汁肉。
culturalBackground: Xi'an's most famous street food. Often called a 'Chinese hamburger'.
seasonalConnection: Year-round Xi'an street food staple.
historicalConnection: Ancient Shaanxi cuisine, dating back to Zhou Dynasty.
steps: **Stew Pork** Braise pork with spices for 2-3 hours until falling apart.
**Make Buns** Make dough, shape into flat rounds, and bake on griddle.
**Chop Pork** Chop meat finely with some fat.
**Assemble** Split bun, stuff with meat.
tips: The bun should be crispy outside, soft inside. Don't skimp on the fat.

name: Yangrou Paomo
description: Xi'an specialty: crumbled flatbread in mutton broth.
chineseDescription: 西安名吃，掰碎的馍配以羊肉汤。
culturalBackground: Xi'an's signature dish. Diners crumble the bread themselves to the desired size.
seasonalConnection: Especially warming in winter.
historicalConnection: Ancient Shaanxi cuisine from Silk Road era.
steps: **Cook Broth** Simmer mutton for 2 hours until tender.
**Crumble Bread** Tear bread into small pieces.
**Assemble** Place bread in bowl. Ladle hot broth over.
**Add** Add vermicelli, cumin, chili, and cilantro.
tips: The bread should be crumbled small to soak up broth properly.

name: Biang Biang Noodles
description: Wide hand-pulled noodles with sizzling chili oil.
chineseDescription: 宽面配以热油泼辣子，香辣过瘾。
culturalBackground: Xi'an's famous wide noodles. The name comes from the sound of slapping dough while pulling.
seasonalConnection: Year-round Xi'an favorite.
historicalConnection: Shaanxi peasant food that became iconic.
steps: **Make Noodles** Mix flour and water. Rest. Pull into wide strips.
**Boil** Cook noodles until chewy.
**Top** Place noodles in bowl. Top with garlic and chili flakes.
**Sizzle** Heat oil until smoking. Pour over chili and garlic.
**Season** Add vinegar and soy sauce.
tips: The hot oil should sizzle when poured. Mix well before eating.

name: Pan-Fried Buns
description: Shanghai breakfast buns with crispy bottom and juicy pork filling.
chineseDescription: 上海早餐代表，底酥馅鲜汁多。
culturalBackground: Shanghai's beloved breakfast. The crispy bottom and soupy filling make it unique.
seasonalConnection: Morning staple in Shanghai.
historicalConnection: Shanghai street food since early 20th century.
steps: **Make Filling** Mix pork with aspic and seasonings.
**Make Dough** Mix flour and water. Rest.
**Wrap** Shape dough, fill, and pleat.
**Pan-fry** Pan-fry with water. Cover to steam.
**Crisp** Uncover to crisp bottoms.
**Garnish** Top with sesame and green onions.
tips: The aspic creates soup inside. Eat carefully - it's hot!

name: Scallion Pancakes
description: Flaky, layered flatbread with scallions.
chineseDescription: 层层起酥的葱香饼。
culturalBackground: Northern Chinese breakfast staple. The layers come from a clever folding technique.
seasonalConnection: Year-round breakfast favorite.
historicalConnection: Traditional Northern Chinese flatbread.
steps: **Make Dough** Mix flour with hot water. Rest.
**Roll** Roll thin. Brush with oil, sprinkle scallions and salt.
**Fold** Roll up like a jelly roll. Coil into spiral.
**Flatten** Flatten spiral into disc.
**Pan-fry** Fry until golden on both sides.
tips: The folding creates layers. Don't skimp on the oil.

name: Red Braised Beef
description: Tender beef braised in soy sauce and spices.
chineseDescription: 酥烂入味的红烧牛肉。
culturalBackground: Hunan style braised beef with a spicy kick from doubanjiang.
seasonalConnection: Warming winter dish.
historicalConnection: Traditional Hunan home cooking.
steps: **Blanch** Blanch beef. Cut into chunks.
**Sear** Brown beef in oil.
**Braise** Add spices, doubanjiang, and water. Simmer 2 hours.
**Serve** Serve with rice or noodles.
tips: Long slow cooking makes the beef tender.

name: Steamed Egg Custard
description: Silky smooth steamed eggs, a comfort food classic.
chineseDescription: 嫩滑如丝的蒸蛋。
culturalBackground: Every Chinese child grows up eating this. Simple yet satisfying.
seasonalConnection: Year-round comfort food.
historicalConnection: Ancient Chinese cooking technique.
steps: **Beat** Beat eggs with water. Strain for smoothness.
**Steam** Steam gently for 10-12 minutes.
**Season** Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil.
**Garnish** Top with green onions.
tips: Low heat and a lid prevent bubbles. Strain for silkiness.

name: Smashed Cucumber with Garlic
description: Refreshing cold cucumber salad with garlic and vinegar.
chineseDescription: 清爽的蒜泥拍黄瓜。
culturalBackground: The ultimate Chinese summer appetizer. Quick, refreshing, and addictive.
seasonalConnection: Summer essential, cooling and refreshing.
historicalConnection: Modern Chinese home cooking.
steps: **Smash** Smash cucumbers with knife. Cut into chunks.
**Season** Toss with garlic, vinegar, soy sauce, and oils.
**Chill** Refrigerate 10 minutes.
**Serve** Serve cold.
tips: Smashing helps the cucumber absorb flavors.

name: Tomato Egg Drop Soup
description: Quick, comforting soup with tomatoes and silky egg ribbons.
chineseDescription: 家常快手汤，番茄酸甜，蛋花嫩滑。
culturalBackground: The most common Chinese home-style soup. Quick, cheap, and comforting.
seasonalConnection: Year-round staple.
historicalConnection: Modern Chinese home cooking.
steps: **Cook Tomatoes** Sauté tomatoes until soft.
**Add Liquid** Add water/stock. Bring to boil.
**Add Eggs** Swirl in beaten eggs gently.
**Season** Add salt and sesame oil.
**Serve** Garnish with green onions.
tips: Swirl eggs gently for beautiful ribbons.

name: Spicy Crawfish
description: Beijing summer specialty: spicy garlic crawfish.
chineseDescription: 北京夏日名吃，麻辣蒜香小龙虾。
culturalBackground: Beijing's summer obsession. Street vendors sell mountains of these every night.
seasonalConnection: Summer night market essential.
historicalConnection: 1990s Beijing street food phenomenon.
steps: **Clean** Purge crawfish in clean water. Remove vein.
**Sauté** Sauté garlic, chilies, and doubanjiang.
**Cook** Add crawfish and beer. Simmer 15 minutes.
**Soak** Let soak in sauce 10 minutes.
**Serve** Serve in shell. Peel and eat.
tips: Let them soak to absorb flavor. Use gloves for peeling.

name: Sugar-Coated Hawthorn
description: Crispy sugar-coated hawthorn berries on a stick.
chineseDescription: 晶莹剔透的糖衣山楂，酸甜可口。
culturalBackground: Beijing's iconic winter street snack. The contrast of crisp sugar and tart fruit is magical.
seasonalConnection: Winter street food, especially during Lunar New Year.
historicalConnection: Southern Song Dynasty imperial snack.
steps: **Prep** Wash berries. Thread onto sticks.
**Caramel** Melt sugar with water until amber.
**Dip** Dip berries quickly in caramel.
**Cool** Place on oiled surface to harden.
tips: Work quickly - the sugar hardens fast. Cool surface prevents sticking.

name: Eight Treasure Rice
description: Festive sticky rice pudding with sweet toppings.
chineseDescription: 节日甜点，糯米配以八种果料。
culturalBackground: Traditional Lunar New Year dessert. The 'eight treasures' symbolize good fortune.
seasonalConnection: Lunar New Year essential dessert.
historicalConnection: Ancient Chinese festival food.
steps: **Soak** Soak rice overnight.
**Steam** Steam rice until cooked.
**Layer** Place treasures in bowl. Add rice and bean paste.
**Steam** Steam again 1 hour.
**Invert** Flip onto serving plate.
tips: Grease the bowl well for easy release.

name: Tangyuan
description: Glutinous rice balls with sweet sesame filling.
chineseDescription: 软糯的糯米汤圆，黑芝麻馅香甜。
culturalBackground: Essential for Lantern Festival (Yuanxiao). The round shape symbolizes family reunion.
seasonalConnection: Lantern Festival (15th day of Lunar New Year) essential.
historicalConnection: Song Dynasty festival food.
steps: **Make Dough** Mix flour with warm water.
**Make Filling** Mix sesame paste, sugar, and lard.
**Shape** Flatten dough, wrap filling, roll into balls.
**Boil** Boil in water until they float.
**Serve** Serve in sweet syrup or plain water.
tips: Don't overfill or they'll burst. Serve hot.

name: Mooncake
description: Traditional Mid-Autumn Festival pastry with lotus seed paste.
chineseDescription: 中秋佳节传统糕点，莲蓉蛋黄馅。
culturalBackground: The symbol of Mid-Autumn Festival. Families share mooncakes while admiring the full moon.
seasonalConnection: Mid-Autumn Festival essential.
historicalConnection: Yuan Dynasty revolutionaries used mooncakes to hide secret messages.
steps: **Make Dough** Mix flour, syrup, and lye water.
**Fill** Wrap paste and yolk in dough.
**Mold** Press into mooncake mold.
**Bake** Bake at 350°F for 20-30 minutes.
**Rest** Let rest 2 days for skin to soften.
tips: Rest the mooncakes for 2 days before eating - the skin softens.

name: Zongzi
description: Sticky rice dumplings wrapped in bamboo leaves.
chineseDescription: 粽叶包裹的糯米粽子，肉馅咸香。
culturalBackground: Dragon Boat Festival essential. Wrapped in bamboo leaves and boiled for hours.
seasonalConnection: Dragon Boat Festival (5th day of 5th lunar month) essential.
historicalConnection: Qu Yuan legend - rice thrown into river to prevent fish from eating his body.
steps: **Soak** Soak rice and leaves overnight.
**Wrap** Form cone with leaves. Add rice, pork, yolk.
**Fold** Fold leaves to seal. Tie with string.
**Boil** Boil 3 hours.
**Serve** Unwrap and eat.
tips: Wrap tightly to prevent leaking. Boil thoroughly.

name: Pork Floss Buns
description: Soft milk buns topped with savory pork floss.
chineseDescription: 松软牛奶面包配以咸香肉松。
culturalBackground: Shanghai bakery favorite. The combination of soft bread and savory floss is addictive.
seasonalConnection: Year-round bakery staple.
historicalConnection: Modern Chinese bakery fusion.
steps: **Make Dough** Mix flour, milk, yeast, and sugar. Knead.
**Proof** Let rise until doubled.
**Shape** Shape into buns. Proof again.
**Bake** Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes.
**Top** Spread mayonnaise, top with pork floss.
tips: The mayonnaise helps the floss stick to the bun.

name: Egg Tarts
description: Flaky pastry shells with silky egg custard.
chineseDescription: 酥皮蛋挞，内馅嫩滑香甜。
culturalBackground: Hong Kong dim sum classic. British custard tarts adapted by Chinese bakers.
seasonalConnection: Year-round dim sum and bakery staple.
historicalConnection: British influence on Cantonese cuisine, 1940s Hong Kong.
steps: **Make Crust** Make flaky pastry. Press into tart molds.
**Make Custard** Heat milk and sugar. Add beaten eggs.
**Fill** Pour custard into shells.
**Bake** Bake at 400°F for 15-20 minutes.
**Serve** Serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: Don't overbake - the custard should still jiggle slightly.

name: Pineapple Buns
description: Sweet buns with crispy pineapple-shaped topping.
chineseDescription: 酥皮甜面包，表面似菠萝纹理。
culturalBackground: Hong Kong bakery icon. The 'pineapple' refers to the cracked topping, not the flavor.
seasonalConnection: Year-round bakery staple, best eaten fresh.
historicalConnection: 1960s Hong Kong bakery invention.
steps: **Make Dough** Make soft bread dough. Proof.
**Make Topping** Mix butter, sugar, flour for crumbly topping.
**Shape** Divide dough. Top with topping mixture.
**Bake** Bake at 375°F until golden and cracked.
**Serve** Serve warm, optionally with butter inside.
tips: The topping should crack during baking - that's the signature look.

name: Turnip Cake
description: Steamed then pan-fried radish cake with cured meats.
chineseDescription: 蒸后煎的萝卜糕，配以腊味。
culturalBackground: Cantonese dim sum essential. Also popular during Lunar New Year.
seasonalConnection: Year-round dim sum, especially popular for Lunar New Year.
historicalConnection: Traditional Cantonese festival food.
steps: **Prep Radish** Grate and squeeze radish.
**Mix** Mix radish, flour, sausage, and shrimp.
**Steam** Steam in loaf pan 45 minutes.
**Cool** Cool completely. Slice.
**Pan-fry** Fry slices until crispy.
**Serve** Serve with chili sauce.
tips: Must cool completely before slicing. Pan-fry for best texture.

name: Taro Cake
description: Steamed taro cake with cured meats and mushrooms.
chineseDescription: 香芋蒸糕，配以腊味和香菇。
culturalBackground: Cantonese dim sum variety, similar to turnip cake but with taro.
seasonalConnection: Year-round dim sum item.
historicalConnection: Traditional Cantonese village food.
steps: **Prep Taro** Cube taro. Steam until soft.
**Mix** Mix taro, flour, sausage, and mushrooms.
**Steam** Steam mixture 45 minutes.
**Cool** Cool and slice.
**Pan-fry** Fry until golden.
**Serve** Serve with chili sauce.
tips: Some taro chunks should remain for texture.

name: Mango Pudding
description: Creamy mango pudding, Hong Kong dim sum dessert.
chineseDescription: 香滑芒果布丁，港式甜品。
culturalBackground: Hong Kong dim sum dessert. Refreshing end to a meal.
seasonalConnection: Summer favorite when mangoes are in season.
historicalConnection: British pudding adapted with tropical mango.
steps: **Blend** Blend mango flesh with coconut milk.
**Dissolve** Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
**Mix** Combine mango mixture with gelatin.
**Chill** Pour into molds. Refrigerate until set.
**Serve** Invert onto plate. Top with fresh mango.
tips: Use ripe, sweet mangoes for best flavor.

name: Black Sesame Soup
description: Warm, nutty black sesame dessert soup.
chineseDescription: 温润香浓的黑芝麻糊。
culturalBackground: Traditional Chinese dessert soup. Believed to nourish hair and kidneys.
seasonalConnection: Winter warming dessert.
historicalConnection: Traditional Chinese medicinal dessert.
steps: **Toast** Toast sesame seeds until fragrant.
**Grind** Grind sesame and rice together.
**Cook** Cook with water, stirring constantly.
**Sweeten** Add rock sugar.
**Serve** Serve warm.
tips: Constant stirring prevents lumps.

name: Red Bean Soup
description: Sweet red bean dessert soup with tangerine peel.
chineseDescription: 陈皮红豆沙，清甜滋润。
culturalBackground: Classic Chinese dessert soup. The tangerine peel adds subtle aroma.
seasonalConnection: Year-round dessert, warming in winter.
historicalConnection: Traditional Cantonese sweet soup.
steps: **Soak** Soak beans 4 hours or overnight.
**Cook** Simmer beans with tangerine peel until soft.
**Mash** Mash some beans for thicker texture.
**Sweeten** Add rock sugar.
**Serve** Serve warm or cold.
tips: The tangerine peel is essential for authentic flavor.

name: Almond Tofu
description: Delicate almond-flavored dessert, not actually tofu.
chineseDescription: 杏仁味的清凉甜品，口感似豆腐。
culturalBackground: A refreshing Chinese dessert. The name comes from its tofu-like texture.
seasonalConnection: Summer cooling dessert.
historicalConnection: Qing Dynasty court dessert.
steps: **Heat** Heat almond milk with sugar.
**Dissolve** Dissolve gelatin in warm milk.
**Chill** Pour into molds. Refrigerate until set.
**Serve** Cut into cubes. Serve with fruit and goji.
tips: Use quality almond milk for best flavor.
